title: Release Breve: Runway & Staffing Cues (May 2026) - Draft
content:
Purpose: A concise, minute-style runbook ("breve") for the May 2026 micro-launch window. This is intentionally short and action-oriented — use this at 48hr, 6hr and 0hr preflight checks. Pull out the staffing cues and the smoke-test commands for the operator pocketcard.

Audience: release conductor, on-call operators, SRE liaison, product manager (observer).

1) TL;DR (30 second):
- Goal: roll out model-routing + locality-optimized cache for Hosted API with minimal disruption and measurable latency improvement for EU region.
- Window: 2026-05-14 00:00 UTC -> 2026-05-16 04:00 UTC (quiet window + 24h watch).
- Safety: staged traffic ramp 0% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with auto-hold on any P50 increase >15% or error rate >0.5% sustained 5m.
- Primary rollback: instant traffic backfill to baseline model variant + kill routing traffic weight.

2) Quick runway checklist (48h -> 0h):
- 48h: confirm feature-flag gates exist (ff:locality-cache-enabled), canary config in platform repo created (PR #4321), telemetry dashboards baked.
- 24h: dry-run smoke on staging with synthetic traffic (seq len distribution matched), validate KV hit rate >= 60% on staging after warm-up.
- 6h: staffing confirmed: primary operator + SRE + model owner + PM. Slack bridge created and pinned.
- 1h: deploy canary lanes to one AZ in eu-west-1 at 0% traffic (deploy-only, no routing). Run quick integration smoke.
- 0m: start traffic ramp per cadence below.

3) Staffing cues (short):
- Primary operator (night shift): owns runbook & smoke checklist, executes traffic ramps.
- SRE liaison: watches infra alarms (CPU/GPU throttles, pod restarts), authorizes next ramp step.
- Model owner: watches quality evals / small sample of recent requests and approves A/B quality snapshot.
- PM / Solutions: on-call for customer-impact comms if rollback.
- Escalation: if SLO breach or silent-queue growth >2x, page on-call (PD: rl_oncall->level2).

4) Ramp cadence (suggested):
- Step 0 (t=+0m): deploy canary (0% traffic) validation (5m).
- Step 1 (t=+15m): 0% -> 10% over 3m. Hold 20m. Telemetry check at 5m/20m.
- Step 2 (t=+40m): 10% -> 50% over 5m. Hold 30m. Check P50/P95, Error rate, KV hit rate trend.
- Step 3 (t=+80m): 50% -> 100% over 10m. Monitor 60m. If all green, exit quiet window for gradual global expansion.

5) Preflight smoke snippets (operator pocket):
- curl -sS -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/generate -d '{"model":"canary-locality","prompt":"smoke test 1"}' | jq '.latency_ms, .error'
- kv-cache check (admin): curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://admin.redwood.ai/cache/status | jq '.kv_hit_rate'
- routing sanity: curl -I https://edge.eu-west-1.redwood.ai/health | grep '200' || echo 'edge-health-fail'

6) Telemetry & thresholds to watch (auto-triggers + manual check):
- Latency: P50 increase >15% or P95 increase >25% over baseline -> HOLD and investigate.
- Errors: user-facing 4xx/5xx rate >0.5% sustained 5m -> ROLLBACK.
- Queue depth: pending request queue growth >2x baseline -> SRE investigate.
- Backend GPU saturation: any GPU util >92% with corresponding increase in latency -> throttle batch size or rollback.
- KV hitrate: if KV hit rate drops below 50% in canary -> likely miswarm, examine warmup sequence.

7) Simple rollback decision matrix (operator friendly):
- Immediate rollback (tactical): any sustained user error rate >0.5% for 5m, or client-facing outage. Execute: set traffic weight to 0 for canary variant, flip ff:locality-cache-enabled -> false (if toggle), notify PD.
- Soft hold + investigate: P95 spike <25% and no error increase. Keep at current weight, run deeper diagnostics (request traces, KV samples). If unresolved in 30m -> rollback.

8) Post-cutover checks (0-24h):
- Confirm KV hit rate stable and latency curve aligned with target.
- Run canary quality eval set (100 sample prompts) and compare BLEU/ROUGE/embedding drift thresholds.
- Watch slow tails (P99) for 6h.
- Draft release note (see template below) and queue for PM review.

9) Release notes draft (copy/edit for final):
Title: Hosted API — Locality-aware caching and routing (May 2026)
Summary: Introduces locality-optimized KV caching and routing to reduce cross-region latency for EU customers. Expected median latency improvement ~12% for eu-west-1. No customer-facing API changes.
What changed: locality-cache-enabled flag, new routing policy for eu-west-1, adjusted cache warmup to prefetch recent prefixes.
Impact/Risks: transient errors possible during warmup window; fallback to baseline model variant is automatic.
Rollout plan: staged traffic ramp across regions with 24h watch.
Docs/links: platform repo PR #4321, operator runbook link (this doc).

10) Communication plan (brief):
- Slack bridge: #release-ops (pin runbook, step cadence).
- Customer comms: Only if rollback or latency impact >20% affecting SLAs. Draft comm if needed: short note with timeline, what we saw, rollback action, and ETA to reattempt.
- Postmortem: required if rollback executed. Owner: model owner + release conductor.

11) Open questions / TODOs: (notes-to-self style)
- Confirm whether KMS key rotation affects admin cache rehydration (Priya to confirm with infra team by 2026-05-06).
- Would a 10m warmup window pre-ramp reduce risk? Quick experiment on staging to validate.
- Verify that canary logs include request-level trace ids by default (Marcus to add agent).

12) Pocket-card for operator (copy this to the pinned slack message):
- 0m: verify canary deployed (0% traffic). run 2 quick smoke commands.
- +15m: ramp to 10% (operator), watch P50/P95, errors. SRE authorize next step.
- +40m: ramp to 50% (operator), hold 30m. model owner runs quality snapshot.
- +80m: ramp to 100%, monitor 60m then exit quiet window.
- Immediate rollback: set canary weight=0, flip ff, notify PD.

Notes: This is deliberately terse. Use the longer release playbook for procedures that require escalation ladders and detailed postmortem templates. Add any immediate observations to the release journal (Jira comment on RELEASE-2147).

-- End of breve --
